children: Sao Paulo police and state prosecutors are investigating Brazilian investment group Grupo Fictor over suspected financial fraud, money laundering and the diversion of investor funds, a source with knowledge of the matter told Reuters on Thursday.
Grupo Fictor, which is under bankruptcy protection, announced plans to buy Banco Master in November last year but abandoned the deal after Brazil's central bank ordered the bank's liquidation.
Authorities are executing 12 search warrants in Sao Paulo and Sao Bernardo do Campo, while courts are freezing 4.3 billion reais ($738.7 million) in assets linked to the group, the source said

The Sao Paulo state government said in a statement, without naming suspects, that police were investigating more than 4 billion reais raised from investors through promises of fixed returns that were not backed by real commercial operations
The investigation uncovered evidence of possible bankruptcy-related crimes, fraud, money laundering and organized crime activity, the government said
Investigators also found possible links to structures examined in other police operations
Grupo Fictor said in a statement it remains at the disposal of authorities to provide clarifications, adding it is dedicated to preserving its operations and defending the interests of its creditors
